    • main

      public MKCScreenHandler.PanelBuilder main()
      Marks this panel as the screen's MAIN panel — its frame (Movement ③). Centred on the screen window; every region(MenuRegion)-anchored sibling resolves against its bounds, exactly as vanilla panels resolve against a menu frame. Exactly one panel per screen should be main().

    • region

      public MKCScreenHandler.PanelBuilder region(MenuRegion region)
      Anchors this panel to the MAIN panel via region (Movement ③) — the same MenuRegion vocabulary vanilla-injected panels use against the menu frame (RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP, BOTTOM_CENTER, …), edge-aware and clamped on-screen. This replaces the retired relative verbs: a side group that was rightOf(MAIN) is now region(MenuRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP), a player inventory below(MAIN) is region(BOTTOM_CENTER), etc.

    • group

      public MKCScreenHandler.PanelBuilder group(String id, Storage storage)
      Adds a structure-only slot group (default priority 100, auto columns).

      Where each kind of "slot behavior" lives

      The group config carries structural behavior — the parts that are a property of the group's place in the menu, not of an individual slot: rightClick(BiConsumer) (group-level right-click handler), pairsWith(String, String) (directional shift-click routing between groups), and the layout knobs (priority / columns / row gap). These stay on the builder because they are group structure.

      Per-slot gating / binding / mending / quick-move is NOT set here — it is armed in THE ONE WINDOW engine by each built slot's MKCSlot.address(), identically to a vanilla slot. On the custom-menu path arm it via Window.slot(MKCScreenHandler.address(panelId, groupId, i)).set(KEY, value) — ideally inside the MKCMenu.Builder.arm hook so it rides the same define chain. (On the container-parity path, the SlotSpec inline verbs — .gate(...), .binding(), .mending(), .quickMove(...) — arm the same keys for you.) An un-armed slot is pure vanilla (engine defaults: gating OPEN, quick-move BOTH, binding/mending off). See MKCBehaviorKeys.

    • pairsWith

      public MKCScreenHandler.PanelBuilder pairsWith(String targetPanelId, String targetGroupId)
      Declares a directional pairing from the last-added group to a target group, identified by "{panelId}.{groupId}". Paired targets sort first in shift-click routing (Layer 1 in MKCScreenHandler.quickMoveStack(Player, int)), ahead of the source-aware baseline and declared priority.

      Exposure-only wrapper over the already-shipped routing semantics (SlotGroup.pairsWith(SlotGroup) + SlotGroup.getPairedWith()). Modeled on rightClick(BiConsumer): replaces the last group config with one that appends a target to its pairing-targets list. The build loop resolves the string references to live SlotGroup instances and wires the pairings before the handler is constructed.

      Call once per target to declare a pairing; multiple calls stack to declare multi-target pairing from the same source group.

    • progressBar

      public MKCScreenHandler.PanelBuilder progressBar(int childX, int childY, int width, int height, DoubleSupplier value)
      Adds a progress bar with a supplier-driven value, left-to-right direction, and default colors. value is a DoubleSupplier returning a normalized 0.0–1.0 progress — the canonical numeric-supplier shape, so a double-valued source feeds it with no box-and-cast. For direction, custom colors, or a label, use .element(new ProgressBar(...)) with the full constructor.

    • tooltip

      public MKCScreenHandler.PanelBuilder tooltip(net.minecraft.network.chat.Component text)
      Attaches a hover tooltip to the MOST RECENTLY added element — the trailing-modifier pattern (mirrors rightClick()/pairsWith() for groups). Closes the gap where the element factories above discard the constructed element, leaving the call site no way to chain .tooltip(...). Every factory builds a library element (an AbstractPanelElement), which carries the tooltip; a raw element(PanelElement) drop-in that is NOT an AbstractPanelElement should set its tooltip in its own construction chain instead.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if called before any element is added, or if the most recent element doesn't support tooltips
